basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 47.' and it opens 'VERS. 47.-- Quem vocavit Laban: Tumulus testis, et Jacob. Acervum testimonii, uterque'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 47.-- Quem vocavit Laban: Tumulus testis, et Jacob. Acervum testimonii, uterque juxta proprietatem | linguae suae. Acervus lingua Hebraea gal dicitur, aad vero testimonium. Rursum lingua Syra acervus igar appellatur, testimonii, sedutha. Jacob igitur acervum testimonii, hoc est Galaad lingua Hebraea appellavit; Laban vero idipsum, hoc est acervum testimonii, igar sedutha gentis suae sermone vocavit. Erat enim Syrus, et antiquam linguam parentum provinciae in qua habitabat, sermone non mutaverat.
